name: AI Regulatory Environment — United States
blurb: Expected AI compliance burden, legal uncertainty and compute access under the US federal-state regime, Oct 2026.
mechanism:
The US regime is permissive at the federal level and fragmented below it. There is no general AI statute and no ex-ante gate outside sectoral pre-market review (FDA). Obligations come from state law — California's frontier transparency act (SB 53), New York's RAISE Act, Colorado's high-risk AI Act, Illinois and NYC employment rules, Texas TRAIGA, California's provenance and companion-chatbot statutes — plus federal content (TAKE IT DOWN), data (state privacy laws, DOJ bulk-data rule) and outbound export controls (BIS).

The defining feature is that the state layer is legally contested. EO 14365 (Dec 2025) stood up a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, ties BEAD funds to avoiding 'onerous' laws, and the US has intervened against Colorado; the bipartisan Great American AI Act draft would preempt state development laws for three years. The model carries this as p_in_force < 1 on the frontier and highrisk slots, which is why contested_share is roughly twice China's: US firms face less expected cost but more of it unpriceable.

Baseline: gross burden ≈ 4.8% of in-scope AI revenue for a $200M reference firm, half of it the fixed cost of mapping ~12 regimes; contested share ≈ 36%. The federal-preemption scenario cuts gross burden ~40% (4.8% → 2.9%), mostly by collapsing the patchwork — preemption is a fixed-cost reform, not a variable-cost one, so it favours small firms disproportionately.

components.name: Shared regulatory-burden graph
components.role: One closed-form graph for every jurisdiction; a jurisdiction is a leaf binding, never a different equation set.

components.name: Instrument catalogue
components.role: Every law, regulation, standard and executive action the slots aggregate, with status, effective date, source and catalogue confidence.

components.name: United States bindings
components.role: Baseline plus counterfactual scenario bindings; each leaf carries its basis inline.

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: United States instrument slots (coverage, cost_share, p_in_force, p_enforced), fragmentation, ex-ante gate, state support, compute supply.

inputs.name: instrument catalogue
inputs.description: instruments.json — the sourced instrument list each slot aggregates.

outputs.name: burden_<slot>
outputs.description: Expected annual compliance cost per instrument slot, as a share of in-scope AI revenue: coverage × cost_share × p_in_force × p_enforced.

outputs.name: gross_burden / net_burden
outputs.description: variable + fixed (patchwork) + ex-ante delay burden; net subtracts state support. Shares of the reference firm's annual AI revenue.

outputs.name: gate_delay_effective_months
outputs.description: Expected launch delay imposed by ex-ante filing/approval, weighted by the gate's coverage and enforcement.

outputs.name: contested_share
outputs.description: Share of the regulatory cost at stake whose legal status is contested (4·p·(1−p) weighting: 1 at a coin flip, 0 when settled). The uncertainty a firm cannot price.

outputs.name: enforcement_gap
outputs.description: Share of in-force obligations that are not enforced in expectation — law on the books an operator can currently underweight.

outputs.name: compute_access / compute_gap
outputs.description: min(1, domestic + licensed × realised + grey) frontier-compute supply against demand. A binding min, not a smooth surrogate.

parameters.description: Pure analytical expectation over instrument slots; no simulation.
Every leaf is a sourced judgement, not a fit. Advisory until graded against compliance-cost actuals.
Weekly; the preemption fight moves faster than the law.

depends_on.note: Same equations.json; outputs are commensurable by construction.
Frontier-slot coverage tracks how concentrated AI revenue is in frontier developers, which the AI Futures milestones condition.
